text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the specific feeding difficulties and when the abdominal distension first became noticeable? Also, has the baby been passing stool regularly, and if so, what does it look like?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the baby passed any stool since birth, and if so, was it delayed for more than 48 hours? Additionally, has there been any vomiting, and if present, is it bilious (green)?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the baby pass thick, ribbon-like stools that require straining or assistance to expel? I would also like to examine the anal sphincter tone and check for a palpable mass in the left lower quadrant.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.
